title: A single Phoenix Labs key can move Liquidity Layer capital: the Prime Relayer is 1-of-2
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1 states that the Prime Relayer Multisig "has the `RELAYER_ROLE` ... and is controlled by Phoenix Labs." Its threshold is "a 1/2 signing requirement" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2) and its signers are "two (2) addresses controlled by Ecosystem Actor Phoenix Labs" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.3).

One signature from one organization is therefore sufficient to exercise the Relayer role. The second key provides redundancy — either address can act if the other is unavailable — not oversight. There is no cross-party check in the fast path at all.

The justification is operational: the Relayer is an automated planner that must act promptly and often, and a multi-party threshold on every rebalance would defeat the purpose. The compensating controls sit elsewhere in the stack — on-chain rate limits bound what a single signature can do, the Freezer can revoke the role, and Sky Governance holds admin.

The honest characterization of the security model is that Spark accepts single-organization, single-key authority over capital movement and contains the consequences rather than preventing the action. That makes rate-limit calibration and Freezer responsiveness the real defences, and it means Phoenix Labs' internal key management is a first-order dependency of the Liquidity Layer — the same Phoenix Labs that is a Nested Contributor with permanent proposal rights and three years of protection against removal.
description: The Prime Relayer Multisig holds RELAYER_ROLE with a 1/2 signing requirement and both signers controlled by Phoenix Labs, so no second party is involved in routine capital movement.
